title: Departure at Dawn
story:
The fire in Mateo's hearth had burned down to a mound of soft, whispering gray ash by the time James opened his eyes. The workshop was quiet, saved only by the early morning sigh of the wind outside the shuttered window. Across the room, the silhouette of the great wooden loom stood like a silent sentinel in the half-light, its long warp threads waiting for the weaver's touch. James sat up, feeling the residual warmth of the hearth in his fur, knowing it was time to move on.

He had known the deep shadows of the Great Canopy, where the trees held the night long after the sun arose. He had known the cold gravel of the Oakhaven outskirts, where the rumbling motor-carriages left their oily breath. He had known the gentle peace of this small hearth, where a stranger had shared his warmth without asking for anything in return. James carefully adjusted his leather strap, running his fingers over the colorful woven threads Mateo had given him, feeling grounded by their texture.

Mateo gave a quiet, sleepy nod from his cot as James made his way to the door. With a soft click of the latch, James stepped out into the crisp, damp morning air. The Plaza of the Fountain was entirely empty, its wide stone basin holding a mirror-like sheet of rainwater that reflected the pale pink and lavender of the dawn sky. He walked past the quiet glass storefronts of the Glass Passage, his small feet making no sound on the washed cobblestones as he began to climb a winding, upward street.

His climb brought him to the base of the Lookout Bridge, a massive stone arch spanning the gap between the town's upper residential terrace and the library hill. James scrambled up the mossy stone steps to the very top of the parapet, where the morning breeze blew fresh and cold. From this high vantage point, the entirety of Oakhaven lay spread out beneath a blanket of low-hanging river mist, its slate roofs glistening like the scales of a sleeping fish.

Perching on the damp stone railing, James reached into his canister and pulled out his smooth green sea-glass. He held it to his eye, looking out over the waking town. Through the emerald lens, the misty stone streets and chimneys transformed into a familiar jungle of towering trunks and leafy canopies, making the strange human world feel, just for a moment, like home. A single white bird rose from the canal below, cutting through the fog, and James watched it go.
